item.title: Dr Cheese revamp :3
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes.

Page Type: SCP Article.

Genre: My design is meant to be spooky, but I may not achieve this factor.

Page Layout: The usual SCP statements, Item Name, Item Class but no picture. Information is going to be structured in the following layout; Appearance description (Height, weight, colour and shape), Discovery (How the anomaly was contained), Abilities (What the anomaly can do, how it does it etc) and the Addendums (Stories about previously explained things).

Elevator Pitch: The basic premise is a tall, slender, arctic hunter with elongated shoulder growths and large elbows, glowing crimson eyes, capable of seeing infrared radiation and heat signature, used for hunting. The anomaly has thousands of tiny muscles on its skin capable of moving guanine crystals to adjust the wavelength of light being reflected off the skin of the anomaly. This is commonly known as camouflage, and is the same method that the Chamaeleonidae (Common Chameleon) uses. Bone marrow scans and nervous axon scans have suggested that overgrowths on the anomaly's shoulder blades and elbows contain many nerve endings, which transfer electrical signals in large amounts to a particular area which creates an electromagnetic field. These electromagnetic pulses disrupt nearby local electric signals. It may use this to alter the function of electrical signals in the brain, or to inhibit power of technology.

Central Narrative: It was a normal day in the UK Arctic Research Facility. It was collection day, where the scientific staff would take a collection of snow for carbon-testing, a process where the amount of carbon that is in a snowflake is collected. Suddenly, the power went out. As the staff stumbled over to the generator, senior researcher Noel Leon noticed a small red glow. Must have been nothing. He got back to fixing the generator and replaced the fuses. But as soon as the generator start-up was initiated, the generator failed. What was going on? Suddenly, pat… pat… pat…. He turned around, but there was nothing but footprints. SNAP. The crunch of his bones in SCP-XXXX's mouth was horrifying, but unheard to remaining staff. As it entered the facility, seven of it's prey had already been frozen. An easy meal. Junior researcher Doctor Edward turned a corner, but the anomaly was gone, just a frozen, half-eaten corpse. He was petrified, and sprinted out to the door and locked it shut. His frozen fingers dialled 911 into a telephone. The rest of the facility was wiped out, with the exception of Doctor Bradly who was obliterated by SCP-XXXX. Doctor Bradly called local authorities and the foundation was alerted. MTF unit Delta-92 Snow-and-Tell was sent to the situation immediately. Using infrared vision, the anomaly's ability was stunted, rendering it useless. Using a Class-3 collapsible containment cell, SCP-XXXX was taken to Site-25 via helicopter with ease.

item.title: JS Staff Post -- Forum Crit -- Info
item.content:encoded:
Author,

Per the required reading forum guidelines, please fill out the concept template to seek feedback on your idea:

 **Seeking Greenlights:** Put yes or no. **Page Type:** SCP Article, Tale, GoI Format, Joke SCP, Site Dossier, Other (specify) **Genre (Optional):** Horror, Drama/Emotional, Comedy, Action, History, Other (specify) **Page Layout (Optional):** [How will you will structure the page in terms of information presentation, or plot development? If you plan on using a unique format/format screw, describe that here.] **Elevator Pitch:** [What is the basic core idea? Use a bullet point list if necessary.] **Central Narrative:** [Describe the story beats or overarching context/"big picture" for your piece. If there is no story content, put "none".] **Hook/Attention-Grabber:** [What is novel/unique about your premise? What is special about your idea here that will make it stand out among the other works already on the mainsite?] **Additional Notes:** [Note any concerns or particular areas of assistance you would like reviewers to focus on.]

Rather than posting a new comment, edit your previous post using the "edit" function under the "options" tab to the lower right of your first comment.

Remember that the combined text for your answers to the last four sections (Elevator Pitch, Central Narrative, Hook/Attention-Grabber, and Additional Notes) MAY NOT exceed 400 words. For convenience, authors can use this page to check wordcount: https://wordcounter.net/

Once you have revised your post accordingly, please reach out to reviewers to request that they look at your thread. You can find example lists of contacts in the Required Reading thread linked above.

item.title: Re: Experience Art In A Whole New Way
item.content:encoded:
You seriously need to expand on this. This is about as bare bones as it gets, and needs a lot. it's an intriguing idea, but:

1) A rescue mission won't be sent in if the MTF is killed.

2) Can outside observers watch what happens or is the painting unaffected as far as they are concerned?

3) This is more of D-Class thing than an MTF thing; most initial exploration is done by D-Class because they are expendable.

4) Is there a reason to explore more than a couple of paintings? While it would be interesting to explore some paintings, I'm not sure that this would be seen as more than a curiosity after a couple of trips.

5) Also, why was it created? Did the person have more than just exploration in mind, or did he want to see how the artist thought? An origin would be nice.

Again, an intriguing idea, but needs to be really expanded on.

item.title: Re: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Writers
item.content:encoded:
Hello hello GiveChocolateNow! Welcome to the Wiki! I'm Ralliston, a site author and a member of the Community Outreach Team - with this helpful little comment, I'll try to help you find your way around the site and link a bunch of useful places and links that will help you in your SCP journey. We're very happy to see the off-site fanbase make their way into the ~official~ SCP Place, by which I of course mean the Wiki. It's also nice to see that you are interested in contributing to the ever-growing amount of articles onsite - I can't wait to see what comes from under your hands!

Without further ado though, let's click the collapsible, shall we? :)

+ show block
– hide block

If you're going to try your hand at writing, try out our Sandbox. You can make yourself a page here to store your drafts, which are in-works articles. Using it, you can link the drafts to reviewers to get their opinions on them before posting. It really helps everyone out a lot.

For brainstorming concepts, try out the Ideas and Brainstorming forum. You can run your ideas by experienced members of the community if you need help refining and fleshing out your concept. It's a very helpful little place for when you want to start your writing journey, especially when you're not sure if the idea is all that great.

If you have a draft ready, make a thread in the Drafts and Critiques forum. Remember to check the stickied posts in the relevant thread for guidelines on how best to use each forum. You can also try the IRC chat for real-time feedback.

From site usage to writing tips, the Guide Hub contains a wealth of resources geared towards helping members produce successful articles. Within the Guides, you will find useful information written by experienced members of the site for the use of newer ones.

The more time you take to familiarize yourself with the SCP style, the drafting process, and the community, the greater your chances are for success! Remember - there is no rush to writing - take your time! The more time you spend on fleshing your ideas out, the more your chance of success becomes!

As far as reading is concerned, you might want to check out Top Rated New Pages, which will display the most popular recent articles. It's helpful to keep up with what's being received well by the community to implement into your very own writing. Alternatively, you might want to look at the User Curated Lists page, where members of the community list and rank their favorite articles in different genres and themes, showing which attempts at such are successful and what the community likes.

Best of luck with your future contributions to the site! I hope you enjoy your time here as much as we do! If you have any more questions, feel free to message me here on Wikidot or on the IRC chats!

item.title: Re: Grant Request For Anti-Fire fire
item.content:encoded:
Alright, thanks for the critique. I've updated the concept to add some conflict and a slightly better ending, I think.

Basically as a result of a mistake during a testing, the Foundation discovered that if the anomalous fire was big enough, it could use itself as fuel, essentially creating an almost perpetually burning fire. This of course resulted in the destruction of a site without casualties because after everything Foundation personnel have dealt with, fire isn't going to be the one that kills them.

Afterward, an architect decided to use this knowledge to create an incinerator using the anomalous fire. This meant that they could store anomalies which needed to be burned constantly while only using minimal fuel. So in the end, that Prometheus scientist's creation was able to be used but not in a way he expected.

What do you think?

item.title: Re: Scp Tv show
item.content:encoded:
I'm seeing a Tales From The Crypt-style anthology series, with a narrator or guide figure presenting that week's cautionary tale. If anybody has seen Yamishibai that's also the sort of flavour I'm talking about, though not every story would have to be unsettling in nature. In the tradition of shows like TFTC, Inside Number 9 and Rick & Morty or even skit shows like The Fast Show you could break from the norm and have a really soulful or emotional episode as a break from all the pan-dimensional craziness and horror.
As I sit here thinking about it I can't get the image of Bobble the Clown as the presenter out of my head. Getting increasingly angry that he has to present these stories instead of his usual fare, perhaps?
Or does Iris takes us into another picture each week?

Side note, any TV series based on the Foundation would be an unbelievably lush garden for Easter Eggs to grow.

item.title: Tales Of Jickery Woe Canon Idea
item.content:encoded:
Hi! I'm new to this site, but not the SCP universe. Here is my idea, in what I hope will become a sprawling Canon.
Synopsis:

Welcome the 1930s. A specialist of biological warfare and weapon design, Jickery Woe, has taken in a destructive anomaly found washed up on the Santa Fe shores, and is preparing it for malicious purposes in the military. The Woe foundation quickly realizes, however, that this creature is unable to be contained. Using tracking devices developed for this creature, they begin to track down others. The Woe foundation struggles to keep the safety and peace of the nation, as SCP's begin to turn up everywhere. The Woe foundation eventually turns into the SCP foundation.

Notes:
While this is an SCP Canon, a big focus is on Jickery and his life.
I need able writers to make this come to pass.
Tell me what you think of this idea!

I teeter between a novote and an upvote. I like the narwhal's anomaly, simple but striking, and I vastly enjoy the escalation of Faeowynn's emails to the Foundation. It recalls SeaWorld's real-life treatment of orcas until recent, and Faeowynn's continued attempts to gain support for Thunderhorn compel me to continue reading.

I don't enjoy the second half as much, though. The interview functions well (though I feel you should remove Everwood's explicit line about bureacracy; given the themes of the work, I understand already that "It's bureaucracy all the way down"), but the ending strikes me as not the right fit. The piece evokes the horrors of bureaucracy's ambivalence toward small fry wonderfully in the emails, but the ending makes the Foundation seem actively malevolent to me which, while I understand the ambivalence makes the Foundation seem malevolent, I feel goes a little overboard.

I noticed that the amount WWS needs to pay to keep Thunderhorn contained originally, $15,321.12, goes ignored for the rest of the piece. If the ending sum that the Foundation fines WWS was closer to that number (not exactly, since that'd be too specific), something like $16,000, I think that would be a good callback to that sum, and make the Foundation's ambivalence more apparent as a cause of evil, rather than a symptom of it.

I'll give it a tentative upvote, since I enjoyed the article overall. +1.

EDIT: Alternatively, you could remove the interview, and make the Foundation's response itself be an email, with the amendment to the Boring Agreement and the fine. That may be more substantial, actually.
